narrative.northStar: A good listener, with a clear plan.
narrative.overview: UserHQ feels human, attentive, and capable. The supplied face mark introduces warmth; precise type, quiet paper surfaces, and clear indigo actions keep attention on customers and the work ahead. This adapts the supplied brand identity to a working application rather than reproducing its brand book.
keyCharacteristics: Clear hierarchy and compact, readable controls.
Customer identity has priority inside tenant portals.

rules.name: The Tenant Identity Rule
rules.body: Product accent overrides continue to own primary actions, foreground contrast, focus rings, and entity avatars. UserHQ brand colors belong to the UserHQ mark and attribution, not a replacement for a customer's logo or name.

rules.name: The Readable Color Rule
rules.body: Body and placeholder text meet 4.5:1 contrast; large text and essential graphical affordances meet 3:1. Never use coral or aqua as small text on white.

rules.name: The Quiet Surface Rule
rules.body: Paper grounds the application. White surfaces and thin neutral boundaries organize content; do not add a shadow to a bordered card. Existing dialogs and popovers retain their functional elevation. Keep decoration out of task surfaces.

dos: Do keep the supplied face and the two-color wordmark consistent.
Do preserve tenant logos, names, accents, and existing behavior.
Do use white working surfaces against the paper background.
Do verify real content, narrow widths, focus, loading, error, and reduced-motion states.
donts: Don't use coral or aqua for low-contrast body text.
Don't turn working screens into decorative marketing compositions.
Don't add fake customer activity, metrics, or product claims.
